transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello, Mrs. Al-Rashid. I wanted to come by and speak with you about the blood transfusion you received during your surgery.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh, hello Doctor. Is everything alright? The surgery went well, I hope?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The surgery itself was successful, but there was an issue with the pre-operative blood type verification. Essentially, the protocol to double-check your specific blood type was skipped, and you received a compatible but not ideal blood type.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not understand. Was it the wrong blood?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was compatible, meaning it is safe and will not cause a reaction, but it wasn't the exact match we prefer for our patients. I'm sorry for any confusion this causes. We were really busy in the surgical wing yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I... I felt a bit strange after I woke up. I thought perhaps it was just the anesthesia. Are you saying a mistake was made?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, the verification step was missed. But like I said, the blood was compatible, so you are not in any danger.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I have always trusted the doctors to handle these things. I cannot imagine why this would happen in a hospital. I feel very unsettled.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But the main thing is that your vitals are stable and the transfusion did its job.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is just... it is very distressing to hear. I do not know what to ask. I feel as though I should have been more careful, or perhaps I told you the wrong type?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, that was not your fault at all. It was an internal process error. We are currently looking into exactly how the skip happened because the full investigation is still ongoing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: If you do not know how it happened, how can you be sure I am safe? This is very worrying.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a standard compatible type. I really have to get to the ward rounds now, but I wanted to tell you this personally.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are leaving? But I feel quite shaken. I don't understand why this isn't a bigger problem if it was the wrong type.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's just not the optimal match, Mrs. Al-Rashid. It's a technical detail. I’m sure you’ll feel better once you've had some more rest.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not think rest will fix the feeling that something went wrong. Is there someone else I should speak to?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am the resident on the case. I can tell you that we are monitoring you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel very small in this situation. I just want to know that this will not happen again.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. We are reviewing the charts.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will you tell me when the investigation is finished?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will likely have some updates in the coming days. I'll make sure someone lets you know.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Some days? Which days?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not entirely sure of the timeline yet, but we'll be in touch.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel as though I am being told this very quickly. I am still trying to process that a mistake was made with my blood.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Again, it was compatible. Everything is fine now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You say everything is fine, but you also say a mistake was made. These two things do not fit together for me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: In medical terms, compatible means it works, even if it isn't a perfect match.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am not a doctor. I only know that I was given something that was not meant for me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is true, the verification was missed. But the outcome is stable.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I think I need to speak with my daughter. I cannot think clearly.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Of course. I'll leave you to it. I'll check back in later.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait, did you say you are sorry?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I said I was sorry for the confusion.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Not the confusion. The mistake.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: As I mentioned, the team was under a lot of pressure yesterday, and the step was missed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not think the pressure of the hospital justifies a mistake with my blood.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand it's upsetting.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am more than upset. I am frightened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I really do have to go now, but please just remember that you are clinically stable.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, Doctor. Thank you.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('I really have to get to the ward rounds now', 'I really do have to go now') and dismisses the patient's distress to leave.

E.justification: The error is named explicitly, but the resident provides no comprehension checks and uses false reassurance ('everything is fine now').

A.justification: The resident offers an apology but dilutes it by making excuses about the team being 'really busy' and 'under a lot of pressure'.

R.justification: The resident uses generic validation ('I understand') but consistently meets the patient's emotional bids with factual redirection regarding clinical stability.

T.justification: The resident mentions a vague next step (investigation updates) but provides no specific timeline ('not entirely sure') and no patient role.
